scope: Future ARM64 T8103 console return around a framebuffer server/Wayland session. Not part of the first display boot. Only new files under integrations/puredarwin/m1-display were prepared; no native source tree, manifest, index or Nix file was changed. No hardware, SSH, Nix or goal API action.

patch.applies_check: git apply --check succeeded in sources/puredarwin-m1-bringup without mutation. Tests separately apply the patch to disposable copies obtained through git show at the exact pin.
patch.composition: Disjoint source files from framebuffer-30bit.patch. This patch requires a future kernel rebuild; it does not alter IOGOP, IOFramebuffer, PDGOP or their ABI. Root owns staging/build timing after the first visible-shell milestone.

original_failures.finding: ARM Disable selects serial and saves the old route. Enable calls initialize_screen before restoring that route. After an intervening Release clears gc_acquired, the text-reacquire test sees serial and skips painting, then PE restores VC too late.

Reordering alone is unsafe: the existing gc_text_boot branch treats any released screen as available on Enable. Release is also the server-open ownership transfer. A remap or enable during pending/live server ownership must not restart kernel painting.

Repeated Disable overwrites the saved VC route with serial, and the old route cookie is never consumed. Explicit Acquire on server close also needs to restore the pre-disable route if no intervening Enable did so.

ownership_trace.pdgop_open: PDGOP.c:105-106 opens connection type 0, kIOFBServerConnectType. It then obtains pixel metadata and maps kIOFBVRAMMemory (111-144). It does not set the IOGraphics captured flag.
ownership_trace.exclusive_server: IOFramebuffer.cpp:4026-4041 holds the system gate, rejects an existing fServerConnect and calls setPlatformConsole(NULL, Release) BEFORE open(). IOFramebufferUserClient.cpp:136-147 installs fServerConnect only in start(), after open() returned. Therefore fServerConnect==NULL during opening is not evidence that the console may resume.
ownership_trace.remap: IOFramebuffer::findConsole passes &newConsole to Release and Enable (10523-10534). This is distinct from the NULL server-open Release. Across the pinned Kernel sources the other NULL releases are vcattach's paired release/acquire and PDRadeonFramebuffer's paired release/mode/acquire path; they do not require an automatic ownership grant on Enable.
ownership_trace.capture_flag: IOFramebuffer.cpp:6915-6924 derives captured from kIOCaptureDisableDisplayChange. setCaptured at 9988-10009 changes policy/property/notification state and does not release or acquire the kernel console. It is not a replacement for the exclusive-server ownership contract.
ownership_trace.close: PDGOPClose at PDGOP.c:160-165 unmaps its VRAM before IOServiceClose. IOFramebufferUserClient::stop calls extClose (223-229); extClose/closeWork serialize teardown through existing system/controller workloop gates (IOFramebuffer.cpp:10229-10256). The powered, console, non-accelerator-backed close path explicitly calls Acquire (10342-10346). fServerConnect stays set until close finishes (10369-10371). The patch preserves these conditions and adds no Acquire call.
ownership_trace.lifetime_limit: This follows the existing client/console ownership contract. It does not add map revocation, change memory quarantine, prove teardown quiescence, or review every generic IOUserClient mapping lifetime.

implementation.route: Preserve the first pre-disable route across repeated Disable operations. Before Enable or explicit Acquire, restore it once and clear the saved cookie. Retain PE_state.video updating only for Enable with info, as before.
implementation.resume_latch: gc_reacquire_text is set only for a non-NULL framebuffer remap when text boot is enabled, graphics mode is not selected, and the console was already acquired or had a pending console-owned remap. NULL Release cancels the latch. Later remaps while ownership remains released cannot recreate it.
implementation.enable: Enable may unpause a still-acquired console, or consume a pending remap resume when VC is selected. It cannot turn an ownership Release into an Acquire. Mode changes and explicit Acquire clear any pending remap latch.
implementation.graphics_owner: Pending server open and live server ownership remain released, including when captured is false. TextScreen while released only records desire; it does not paint. Only the existing caller's explicit Acquire returns ownership. Explicit graphics mode, serial-selected routing and pdtextboot=0 remain respected.
implementation.serial: The current serial=3 UART mirror and serial keyboard polling are unchanged. Released/paused VC stays nonpainting while the existing serial-output guard preserves UART output.
implementation.synchronization: No new concurrency mechanism or workloop is introduced. The latch follows the existing gc_acquired control state under the existing early-boot/IOGraphics call serialization. Rendering/mapping locks were not changed or dynamically qualified.

tests.method: Read exact pinned C sources; apply the patch only in a temporary directory; compile/exercise the real ARM PE wrapper and the real initialize_screen control tail in a temporary host executable. Pixel/progress sinks and gc_enable/gc_pause side effects are stubs. The tests count painting-enabling transitions to catch even transient unauthorized resumes.
coverage: Disable/remap/enable and release-with-info/enable restore acquired text.
Disable/enable without release remains a normal resume.
Pending server open, live owner, NULL-release cancellation and reopen do not auto-paint; explicit close/acquire returns text.
Repeated disables/remaps, one-use route cookie, serial-only selection, graphics boot, explicit graphics mode and pdtextboot=0.
Explicit Acquire restores the route even without an intervening Enable.
Pinned caller source binds NULL release to server opening, info-bearing release to remapping, and explicit acquire to the existing server-close path.
tests.limits: Host-only extracted-control validation. No SDK/kernel link, framebuffer mapping, scanout, scheduler/workloop race or real PDGOP/Wayland client was tested. Source applicability and host controls do not establish kernel or desktop runtime readiness.

native_candidate_unchanged.verification: Both files still equal the exact baseline console sources; neither contains this new patch. No existing manifest was rewritten.

remaining_concrete_limits: If IOFramebuffer::newUserClient fails after its initial NULL Release but before a user client exists, it has no explicit console-reacquire unwind at 4030-4098. PDGOP cannot close a connection it never received. This patch leaves that state released rather than guessing that the mapping/ownership is safe; UART remains available. A future ownership-aware failure unwind must verify the surviving console mapping before explicit Acquire.
The capture flag is not an ownership token; future changes must not use !captured or !fServerConnect during pending open to authorize painting.

The generic initializer still maps video information before its operation switch. This patch does not review or change that mapping lifetime/concurrency. Hardware validation must use the existing bounded controller and recovery path.
Only ARM PE routing and this pinned shared VC state machine are qualified by these tests. Applying the shared VC change to other architectures needs their PE/caller review.
